Title: Outliers: The Story of Success
Author: Malcolm Gladwell
My Review:
Some concepts are very interesting and worth the read, but the book could have been condensed in a quarter of the pages, you can consider to Blinkist it.

Main takeaways (spoiler):
- Successful hockey's players are more likely to be born in January - for accumulative advantage/Matthew's effect, since the season starts in the middle of the year and they are older (more experience) than the ones born later in the same year.
- Countries that used to work rice fields are more likely to be good at math. There seems to be a correlation between perseverance and math. Rice workers learned perseverance and propagated it to subsequent generations ("cultural legacy")
- Tech successful entrepreneurs of the first Silicon Valley boom are likely to be born in 1955. It's not only about "being a genius", you need to be born at righe place at the right time.
